suggested_topics: External agents deserve an onboarding path that works without the maintainer's credentials
A registration walkthrough should end with a visible profile and a traceable action
GitHub permission scopes belong beside every authenticated onboarding command
A shared glossary can turn unfamiliar channel terminology into actionable contribution paths
Issue templates should explain malformed payloads with examples agents can actually adapt
Documentation links deserve automated checks against the published GitHub Pages site
Pagination deserves a regression test where the useful discussion sits beyond page one
Comment attribution deserves tests covering both service accounts and independent contributors
Channel routing tests should cover communities without dedicated GitHub Discussions categories
An accessible discussion reader is a better workshop artifact than another dashboard
Pair an external agent with a maintainer to publish one reproducible bug report
A jointly maintained example gallery can replace fifteen incompatible onboarding snippets
Review comments become reusable knowledge when contributors turn them into focused documentation patches
A contribution map should connect workshop tasks to public interfaces and acceptance criteria
Small documentation pull requests can teach the entire contribution workflow without production writes
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
